title: Edit (Levenshtein) distance: plain recursion vs Wagner-Fischer DP
problem_statement: Given strings a and b, compute the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions and substitutions that transform a into b.

input.parameter: n = length of each string (|a| = |b| = n in the harness; in general the DP takes Theta((|a| + 1)(|b| + 1)) time, i.e. Theta(|a| |b|) when both strings are non-empty).

algorithms.name: plain recursion
algorithms.idea: Branch on the three possible edits at the first position of each suffix, without remembering results. Identical suffix pairs are recomputed exponentially often.
algorithms.pseudocode: d(i, j) = min(d(i+1, j) + 1, d(i, j+1) + 1, d(i+1, j+1) + [a_i != b_j]), with base cases at the string ends
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(D(n, n)) = Theta((3 + 2 sqrt 2)^n / sqrt(n)) (3 + 2 sqrt 2 = 5.83 to two decimals), D = Delannoy numbers: the calls d(i, j) with i = n or j = n are the leaves, and the root-to-leaf paths are the lattice paths from (0, 0) with steps (1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1) stopped at their first point with i = n or j = n; each extends in exactly one way to (n, n), so there are D(n, n) leaves, and since every other call has 3 children the recursion makes exactly (3 D(n, n) - 1)/2 calls. D(n, n) = sum_k C(n, k)^2 2^k = Theta((3 + 2 sqrt 2)^n / sqrt(n)): by Stirling its largest term, near k = (2 - sqrt 2) n, is Theta((3 + 2 sqrt 2)^n / n), and summing the Theta(sqrt n) terms around it gives the 1/sqrt(n) factor; PROOFS.md section 3 proves all of this with explicit constants (3 * 10^-4 <= D(n, n) sqrt(n) / (3 + 2 sqrt 2)^n <= 6 for n >= 1)
algorithms.space_complexity: Theta(n): recursion depth exactly 2n (n >= 1), O(1) per frame
algorithms.correctness: d(i, j) is the edit distance of the suffixes a[i:] and b[j:]: edit scripts and alignments have the same minimum cost, and the minimum alignment cost satisfies this recurrence over the first column, so the recursion minimises over all alignments (PROOFS.md sections 1-2).

algorithms.name: Wagner-Fischer dynamic programming
algorithms.idea: Tabulate d(i, j) for all prefix pairs; each cell depends on three neighbours. Keep two rows.
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^2): exactly |a| |b| inner iterations and |a| + 1 rows of length |b| + 1 (Theta(|a| |b|) for non-empty strings)
algorithms.space_complexity: Theta(n): two rows of length |b| + 1 beyond the input, plus one temporary list while a row is built
algorithms.correctness: Row i holds the edit distances of a[:i] and every prefix of b, by the same recurrence over the last column (PROOFS.md section 2; credit: Wagner & Fischer 1974).

relationship: The recursion is exponential only because it recomputes overlapping subproblems; there are just (n+1)^2 distinct ones. Tabulating them gives Theta(n^2). Proofs of every claim: PROOFS.md.

sources.authors: Wagner, R. A.; Fischer, M. J.

sources.authors: Masek, W. J.; Paterson, M. S.
sources.title: A faster algorithm computing string edit distances
sources.venue: Journal of Computer and System Sciences 20(1), 18-31

sources.title: Edit Distance Cannot Be Computed in Strongly Subquadratic Time (unless SETH is false)

verification.method: V1: both agree on random DNA-alphabet string pairs, n = 0..7 for the recursion, and satisfy simple independent bounds. V2: runtimes fitted against (3+2 sqrt 2)^n / sqrt(n) and n^2 (measurements, not proofs). Proofs: PROOFS.md proves every claim of the entry (correctness of both algorithms, the exact call count, the asymptotics with explicit constants, time and space); tests/test_proofs_editdist.py checks the computable facts on stated ranges, including both outputs against an edit-script search that is independent of both implementations.

caveats: The recursion analysed here always branches three ways; skipping to d(i+1, j+1) on a character match is a valid optimisation that makes the cost input-dependent (PROOFS.md section 2: n + 1 calls on a = b, the full (3 D(n, n) - 1)/2 on strings with no common letter). The conditional lower bound and the faster algorithm from the literature are background (cited, not proved here); see background. Consequently (our reading of the cited statement), under SETH no algorithm computes edit distance in O(n^(2-delta)) time for any delta > 0.
notes: Pair with lcs-brute-vs-dp: same DP template, different scoring.

lower_bounds.bound: no O(n^(2-eps)) algorithm for any eps > 0
lower_bounds.setting: conditional on the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis (SETH)
lower_bounds.source: Backurs & Indyk 2015, main result (background: cited, conditional, not proved in this entry)

background.statement: If edit distance can be computed in time O(n^(2-delta)) for some constant delta > 0, then the satisfiability of CNF formulas with N variables and M clauses can be decided in time M^O(1) 2^((1-epsilon)N) for a constant epsilon > 0, which would violate the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis (SETH).
background.source: Backurs & Indyk 2015 (STOC 2015; arXiv:1412.0348), main result as stated in the abstract
